mainTopic: Rules for making תפילין: the order of the passages, features that are a הלכה למשה מסיני, strap color, square shape, and torn compartment walls
overview: This amud opens in the middle of אביי's rule about switching the four passages in the head-תפילין, and רבא argues that any switch at all makes them פסול. The גמרא then lists parts of the תפילין that are a הלכה למשה מסיני: the base (תיתורא), the strap passage (מעברתא) and the letter שי"ן. אביי and רב דימי מנהרדעא disagree twice: whether the groove between compartments must reach the stitches, and whether the parchment must be checked before writing. רבי יצחק says black straps are a הלכה למשה מסיני. A ברייתא allowing other colors seems to contradict him. The גמרא answers that the outside of the strap must be black, while the inside may be any color except red. Next, a ברייתא teaches that תפילין must be square, and רב פפא explains what that means. Finally, רב הונא, רב חסדא and רבא discuss when torn inner walls make head-תפילין פסול, and רב יוסף gives a test for telling new תפילין from old.

steps.title: Only switching inner and outer passages is a problem
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits his ruling. Switching the passages makes the תפילין פסול only when an inner passage trades places with an outer one. Switching two inner passages, or two outer ones, is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said the תפילין are פסול when an inner passage is switched with an outer one, or an outer one with an inner one. But if an inner one is switched with the other inner one, or an outer one with the other outer one, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is finishing his statement about switching the order of the passages in the head-תפילין. He says only some switches make them פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head-תפילין hold four passages in a set order. Two sit on the outside edges and two sit in the middle. אביי's idea is that what matters is whether a passage sits on the outside or the inside, so trading two passages of the same type does no harm.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner passages, the two that sit in the middle compartments
The outer passages, the two that sit in the end compartments
We have no problem with it; it is fine

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The words before it (on the previous עמוד) are אביי saying 'we only said that switching the passages makes them פסול when…'. So this is a limit on that ruling, not a new topic.

phrases.english: only an inner passage for an outer one
phrases.notes: This finishes אביי's rule from just before: we only said switched passages are פסול when it's an inner one put in place of an outer one.

phrases.english: or an outer passage for an inner one,
but an inner passage for the other inner one
or an outer passage for the other outer one, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גַּוָּיְיתָא לְבָרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's qualification of the rule that switched passages make תפילין פסול (begun before this section).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only switching between inner and outer positions makes the תפילין פסול. Swapping two passages of the same type is fine.

steps.title: רבא argues that every switch puts a passage on the wrong side
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why אביי's distinction should matter. Swapping the two outer passages also puts each one facing the wrong side, right instead of left and left instead of right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: What is different about switching an inner passage with an outer one, or an outer one with an inner one, that makes it not valid? It is because the passage that needs to 'see the air' (sit on the outer edge) does not see it, and the one that does not need to see the air does see it. But when you switch outer with outer, or inner with inner, the same problem exists. The passage that needs to see the air of the right side sees the air of the left, and the one meant for the left sees the air of the right!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's limit. He argues that swapping two passages of the same type also puts them in the wrong place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא first spells out אביי's reason: an outer passage must face the open air, and an inner passage must not. Then he points out that each outer passage has its own fixed side. So swapping the two outer ones still breaks the required order, just in a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? A question that challenges a distinction
To 'see the air': to sit on the outer edge, facing outside

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
What is different about an inner passage for an outer one
and an outer one for an inner one, that they are not valid?
It is because this passage, which needs to see the air,
does not see it,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דְּלָא קָא בָעֵי לְמִיחְזֵי אַוֵּירָא
phrases.english: and that passage, which does not need to see the air,
does see it.
But outer for outer, or inner for inner, should be the same:
this passage, which needs to see the air of the right side,
sees the air of the left side,
and the one meant for the left sees the air of the right!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction אביי drew in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that swapping two passages of the same type is acceptable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the problem is a passage facing the wrong way, a same-type swap also makes each passage face the wrong side (right and left are reversed). So it should be פסול too.

steps.title: There is no difference: any switch is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that every change in the order of the passages makes the תפילין פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws the conclusion of his challenge. Every switch is the same, and all of them make the תפילין פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This throws out אביי's limit from step 1. The order of all four passages is fixed, so any change at all disqualifies the תפילין.
steps.whatToRemember: In the head-תפילין, every one of the four passages has a fixed place. According to רבא, switching any two of them makes the תפילין פסול.

phrases.english: Rather, there is no difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes רבא's challenge in step 2 by rejecting אביי's distinction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any change in the order of the passages makes the תפילין פסול.

steps.title: The base of the תפילין is a law given to משה at סיני
steps.stepSummary: רב חננאל quotes רב: the תיתורא, the base of the תפילין, is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חננאל said in the name of רב: The תיתורא of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It lists physical parts of the תפילין that are required by a הלכה למשה מסיני, starting with the base.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תיתורא is the flat base that the compartments sit on. Calling it a הלכה למשה מסיני means it is not learned from a פסוק but comes from a teaching passed down from משה.

keyTerms.meaning: The base of the תפילין that the box sits on
A law handed down orally from משה at סיני

steps.whyThisMatters: Because it is a הלכה למשה מסיני, תפילין without this base would not be kosher.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥananel said that Rav said:
The base of the tefillin
is a law given to Moses from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: required physical features of the תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תיתורא is required by a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: The strap passage is a law given to משה at סיני
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the מעברתא, the passage for the strap, is also a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The מעברתא of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a second required part of the תפילין to the list: the passage the strap goes through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מעברתא is the part of the base that the strap is threaded through. אביי adds it to the list of features required by a teaching from סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: The passage in the base of the תפילין that the strap goes through

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The strap passage of the tefillin
is a law given to Moses from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַעְבַּרְתָּא דִּתְפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second feature to the list begun in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מעברתא is required by a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: The letter שי"ן is a law given to משה at סיני
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the letter שי"ן on the תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: The שי"ן of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי names a third feature: the letter שי"ן on the head-תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שי"ן is shaped into the leather on the outside of the head-תפילין. Like the base and the strap passage, it is required by a teaching from סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter shin formed on the outside of the head-תפילין

steps.whatToRemember: Three parts of the תפילין are a הלכה למשה מסיני: the תיתורא (base), the מעברתא (strap passage), and the שי"ן.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
The letter shin of the tefillin
is a law given to Moses from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שִׁי״ן שֶׁל תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third feature to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שי"ן on the תפילין is required by a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: The groove must reach down to the stitches
steps.stepSummary: אביי continues: the groove between the compartments must go all the way down to where the box is stitched to the base.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the groove must reach the place of the stitches.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds another rule about the shape of the head-תפילין: how deep the separating groove must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head-תפילין has four compartments separated by grooves. אביי requires each groove to run all the way down to the stitches at the base, so the compartments are fully separated.

keyTerms.meaning: The groove separating the compartments of the head-תפילין
The stitching that attaches the box to its base

phrases.english: And the groove must reach
phrases.notes: אביי is still the one speaking here.

phrases.english: the place of the stitches.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ חָרִיץ לִמְקוֹם הַתֶּפֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's rules about the physical shape of the תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The groove between compartments must reach down to the stitches.

steps.title: רב דימי: a visible groove is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא disagrees. As long as the groove is clearly visible, it does not need to reach the stitches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי מנהרדעא said: Since it is noticeable, it is not necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי מנהרדעא gives a different view from אביי's rule in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב דימי, the point of the groove is to show that there are separate compartments. If the separation can clearly be seen, the groove does not have to go all the way down to the base.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on the groove. אביי says it must reach the stitches. רב דימי says it is enough if the separation is clearly visible.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi of Neharde'a said:
Since it is noticeable, it is not necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא אָמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּמִנְּכַר, לָא צְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the requirement stated in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the groove is clearly visible, it does not need to reach the stitches.

steps.title: אביי says the parchment must be checked before writing
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the parchment for תפילין must be checked for holes before the scribe writes on it, because the writing has to be complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי also said: the parchment of תפילין must be checked first, because it might have a flaw, and we need complete writing, which would be missing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another rule about making תפילין. Before writing, the scribe must check the parchment for small holes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole under a letter would mean the letter is not fully written, and תפילין need complete writing. So אביי says you cannot just start writing. You must check the parchment first.

keyTerms.meaning: Parchment (קלף), the material the פרשיות are written on
A flaw or weakness, here a small hole
Complete, whole writing, with no part of a letter missing

phrases.english: And אביי said:
This parchment of תפילין
needs to be checked,
because perhaps it has a flaw in it,
phrases.notes: The flaw here means a tiny hole in the parchment.

phrases.english: and we require complete writing, and it would be missing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another rule from אביי in his list of rules about making תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The parchment for תפילין must be checked for holes before writing.

steps.title: רב דימי מנהרדעא says the quill does the checking
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא disagrees with אביי. No check is needed beforehand, because the quill shows any problem while writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא said: there is no need; the quill checks it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי מנהרדעא argues with אביי again, just as he did in Step 8. He says there is no need to check the parchment ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As the scribe writes, the quill moves over the parchment. A hole that the ink covers is not a problem, and a real problem would show up while writing. So a separate check beforehand is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The quill or pen the scribe writes with

phrases.english: רב דימי of נהרדעא said:
It is not necessary,
the quill checks it.
phrases.notes: He means the writing itself shows whether the spot is good, so no separate check is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא אָמַר: לָא צְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's rule in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No check is needed before writing; the quill reveals any problem.

steps.title: רבי יצחק says black straps are a tradition from סיני
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that the straps of תפילין must be black, and that this is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: black straps are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule about the straps begins. רבי יצחק says the rule that the straps must be black goes back to משה at סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds to the list of תפילין rules that are הלכה למשה מסיני. Because a הלכה למשה מסיני is a firm requirement, any other color would seem to be not allowed. That is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The leather straps of the תפילין

phrases.english: רבי יצחק said:
Black straps
are a law given to משה at סיני.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: רְצוּעוֹת שְׁחוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the box and parchment to the straps, still listing rules that are הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The straps of תפילין must be black, as a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that the straps of תפילין are black.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows green and white straps too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק with a ברייתא that allows green, black, or white straps and forbids only red.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: תפילין may only be tied with their own kind, whether green, black, or white. Red ones he should not make, because of disgrace and because of something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to contradict רבי יצחק. It allows several colors of straps, not only black.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If black straps were a הלכה למשה מסיני, green and white should not be allowed. Yet the ברייתא allows them and forbids only red, for reasons of appearance. So the ברייתא seems to argue against רבי יצחק. Step 18 answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: With their own kind, meaning straps made of hide like the תפילין themselves
Literally 'something else,' a polite way of hinting at something unpleasant

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא forbids red straps because red is like black. It forbids red only because of how it looks. The challenge is that green and white are allowed, which seems to clash with requiring black.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִילִּין אֵין קוֹשְׁרִין אוֹתָן אֶלָּא בְּמִינָן,
phrases.english: תפילין may be tied only with their own kind,
phrases.notes: The straps must be made of hide, like the תפילין themselves.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין יְרוּקּוֹת בֵּין שְׁחוֹרוֹת בֵּין לְבָנוֹת,
phrases.english: whether green, or black, or white,
but red ones he should not make,
because of disgrace and because of something else.
phrases.notes: Red straps might look like blood from a wound on his head. 'Something else' politely hints that people might suspect something improper about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יצחק's rule in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that black straps are a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows green and white straps, which should not be allowed if black is required by a law from סיני.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's story: רבי עקיבא's student used תכלת strips
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the ברייתא, רבי יהודה tells of a student of רבי עקיבא who tied his תפילין with strips of תכלת wool, and argues that רבי עקיבא would not have stayed silent if it were wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was a story about a student of רבי עקיבא who tied his תפילין with strips of תכלת, and רבי עקיבא said nothing to him. Is it possible that this righteous man saw his student and did not stop him?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a story from רבי יהודה. He suggests that tying תפילין with wool strips must be allowed, because רבי עקיבא did not object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's proof rests on silence. A great צדיק like רבי עקיבא would surely have stopped his student from doing something wrong. So the fact that he said nothing seems to show that straps not made of hide are acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: A story about something that actually happened

phrases.english: רבי יהודה said:
There was a story with a student of רבי עקיבא
who used to tie his תפילין
with strips of sky-blue wool,
and he said nothing to him.
phrases.notes: The one who said nothing is רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Is it possible that this righteous man saw his student
and did not stop him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּתַלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא quoted in Step 12, now with a story.
steps.raayaObject: That tying תפילין with strips not made of hide is acceptable
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's silence when his student tied his תפילין with תכלת strips

steps.title: The answer: רבי עקיבא never saw it
steps.stepSummary: Another Sage rejects the proof. רבי עקיבא did not see what the student did, and if he had seen it, he would not have allowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. He did not see him, and if he had seen him, he would not have let him.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone answers רבי יהודה and knocks down his proof from silence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence proves something only if the teacher knew about it. Here רבי עקיבא simply did not see it. So the story shows nothing, and the student was in fact doing something wrong.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Yes' here means 'yes, it is possible.' It does not agree with רבי יהודה. It means the student really could have done wrong without רבי עקיבא stopping him.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
phrases.notes: He means yes, it is possible, because רבי עקיבא never knew about it.

phrases.english: he did not see him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם רָאָה אוֹתוֹ לֹא הָיָה מַנִּיחוֹ.
phrases.english: and if he had seen him, he would not have let him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הֵן, לֹא רָאָה אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's proof in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Silence proves nothing if רבי עקיבא never saw what happened.

steps.title: A second story: הורקנוס used purple wool strips
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells of הורקנוס, son of רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס, who tied his תפילין with purple wool strips, and asks again how his righteous father could have stayed silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with הורקנוס, son of רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס, who tied his תפילין with strips of purple wool, and his father said nothing to him. Is it possible that this righteous man saw his son and did not stop him?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second story with the same kind of proof. This time a son used purple wool and his father said nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument works the same way as Step 13. A צדיק like רבי אליעזר would surely correct his own son. So his silence seems to show that wool strips are acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: That righteous man, a respectful way of referring to the great teacher

phrases.english: There was a story with הורקנוס,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן הוּרְקָנוֹס,
phrases.english: the son of רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס,
who used to tie his תפילין
with strips of purple wool,
and he said nothing to him.
phrases.notes: The one who said nothing is his father, רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Is it possible that this righteous man saw his son
and did not stop him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּהוּרְקָנוֹס בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן הוּרְקָנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story in the same ברייתא, with the same kind of proof as Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That tying תפילין with wool strips is acceptable
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's silence when his son used purple wool strips

steps.title: The same answer: the father never saw it
steps.stepSummary: The Sages reject this proof too. רבי אליעזר did not see what his son did, and he would have stopped him if he had.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Yes. He did not see him, and if he had seen him, he would not have let him.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages give the same answer as before, and this ends the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, silence proves nothing when the teacher did not know what was happening. Both stories show only what someone did, not that it was allowed. The ברייתא still allows green, black, or white hide straps, so the challenge to רבי יצחק from Step 12 still stands. The גמרא returns to it in step 17 and answers it in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not see him; he did not know what was happening

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק says black straps are a הלכה למשה מסיני. A ברייתא seems to allow green and white straps too and forbids red. Its two stories of wool strips do not prove anything, because the teachers simply never saw what happened. The גמרא answers the challenge to רבי יצחק in step 18.

phrases.english: They said to him: Yes,
he did not see him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם רָאָה אוֹתוֹ לֹא הָיָה מַנִּיחוֹ.
phrases.english: and if he had seen him, he would not have let him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הֵן, לֹא רָאָה אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 15, the same way Step 14 rejected Step 13.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר never saw his son doing it, so his silence shows nothing.

steps.title: Back to the challenge: the ברייתא allows several colors
steps.stepSummary: After the stories, the גמרא returns to the main point of the ברייתא: green, black and white straps are all allowed, which seems to clash with רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches that the straps may be green, black, or white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the stories aside and brings back the core of its challenge against רבי יצחק. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק said black straps are a הלכה למשה מסיני. The ברייתא allows green and white too, so the clash is now stated clearly and needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case; anyway (setting other points aside)

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
phrases.notes: The stories about the students were pushed away, but the ברייתא's basic rule still stands, and that rule is the problem.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין יְרוּקּוֹת בֵּין שְׁחוֹרוֹת וּבֵין לְבָנוֹת.
phrases.english: whether green, or black, or white.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories of steps 13-16 and goes back to the challenge from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that תפילין straps must be black as a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly allows green and white straps, so black cannot be required.

steps.title: Inside of the strap vs. outside of the strap
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction: the ברייתא is talking about the inside of the strap, and רבי יצחק is talking about the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it means the inside; there it means the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the strap into two sides. Each source is talking about a different side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's "any color except red" applies to the inner side that touches the body. רבי יצחק's requirement of black applies to the outer side that people see. So both rules can be true together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... there (each source is about a different case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical rule that the outer side of תפילין straps must be black.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it means on the inside,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the ברייתא that allows other colors; the inside is the side touching the body.

phrases.english: there, it means on the outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן – מִבִּפְנִים, כָּאן – מִבַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: each source talks about a different side of the strap.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא and רבי יצחק were talking about the same strap surface and disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about the inside, which may be any color but red; רבי יצחק is about the outside, which must be black.

steps.title: Why would red matter on the hidden inside?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is about the inside, which no one sees, why does it forbid red because of disgrace and "something else"?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is the inside, what disgrace or "other matter" is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at its own answer. The ברייתא's reasons against red seem to fit only something people can see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא banned red because of גנאי and a דבר אחר. Both of these are worries about how it looks. But if the red is on the inside, no one sees it, so the reasons seem not to apply.

keyTerms.meaning: "Something else": a polite way of hinting at another problem without naming it

phrases.english: If it is on the inside,
what disgrace or "other matter" is there?
phrases.notes: These are the two reasons the ברייתא gave for banning red straps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִבִּפְנִים, מַאי גְּנַאי וְדָבָר אַחֵר אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inside/outside answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is talking about the inside of the strap.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's reasons are about appearance, and the inside cannot be seen.

steps.title: Straps sometimes flip over
steps.stepSummary: The inside can become visible, because the straps sometimes turn over.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes the straps turn over on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the inside is not always hidden. When the strap twists, the inner side shows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because straps flip, the inner color will sometimes be seen. So the worries about how red looks still apply to the inside, and the inside/outside answer stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Outside of the strap: must be black. Inside: any color except red, since straps can flip and the red would show.

phrases.english: Sometimes they turn over on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין דְּמִתְהַפְכִין לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: the hidden side does not always stay hidden.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The inside is never seen, so its color cannot cause disgrace.
steps.terutzMaskana: The straps flip, the inside shows, so red is banned there too.

steps.title: תפילין must be square
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the square shape of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: square תפילין are a law given to משה at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: the shape of the תפילין boxes. It brings a ברייתא saying they must be square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not learned from a פסוק. It is an oral law passed down from משה, just like רבי יצחק's rule about black straps.

keyTerms.meaning: A law told orally to משה at סיני, not written in the תורה

phrases.english: It was taught: square תפילין
are a law given to Moses at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: תְּפִילִּין מְרוּבָּעוֹת – הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from the straps to the shape of the boxes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילין must be square, as a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Square along the seams and the diagonals
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the square requirement applies to the stitching and to the diagonals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: square at their seams and their diagonals.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains what "square" means for תפילין. He names the exact places that must be square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough to look roughly square. The stitched seams must form a square, and the diagonals must match, which is how you know the corners are true right angles.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
at their seams and at their diagonals.
phrases.notes: He means both the sewn edges and the corner-to-corner lines must come out square.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּתִפְרָן וּבַאֲלַכְסוֹנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the term "square" from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The square requirement covers both the seams and the diagonals.

steps.title: A משנה about round תפילין seems to support the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה saying round תפילין are dangerous and invalid supports the square rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports it: one who makes his תפילין round faces danger and does not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to find support for the square rule in a משנה. The משנה says round תפילין do not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If round תפילין are not a מצוה, it may be because תפילין must be square. That would back up the ברייתא of step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him

phrases.english: Let us say this supports it:
one who makes his תפילין round
there is danger, and there is no מצוה in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support the rule of step 21 from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that תפילין must be square.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מגילה that round תפילין are dangerous and do not fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: The משנה means nut-shaped תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the proof: the משנה is about תפילין shaped like a nut, which is a different problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the משנה is about תפילין made like a nut.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes away the proof from the משנה. He says the משנה is talking about a very specific round shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Round" in the משנה means fully rounded like a nut, which is also why it is dangerous. That says nothing about flat-bottomed תפילין that just are not square, so the ברייתא is still needed to teach the square rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the משנה being discussed

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא does not argue with the square rule. He only says this משנה is not proof for it, because it is about a different shape.
steps.whatToRemember: תפילין must be square (a הלכה למשה מסיני). The משנה about round תפילין is about nut-shaped ones, so it does not prove the square rule.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The משנה is about ones made like a nut.
phrases.notes: A nut shape is rounded all over, which explains the "danger" part of the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַתְנִיתִין דַּעֲבִידָא כִּי אַמְגּוּזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not the square rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה is about nut-shaped תפילין, so it cannot show that non-square תפילין with a flat bottom are invalid.

steps.title: Torn head-תפילין are valid while the outer surface is whole
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that תפילין stay כשר as long as the outer face of the box is intact.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: תפילין are valid as long as the outer surface of the box is still whole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a rule from רב הונא about damaged תפילין. If the outside face of the box is not torn, the תפילין are still כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is head-תפילין, which have four compartments with leather walls between them. רב הונא says a tear inside the box, in those walls, does not matter. All that counts is that the outer face is whole.

keyTerms.meaning: The face (outer surface) of the תפילין box

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Tefillin, as long as
the face of the box is intact, are valid.
phrases.notes: He means even if the leather walls inside, between the compartments, have torn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: תְּפִילִּין, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁפְּנֵי טַבְלָא קַיֶּימֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, torn תפילין, after the discussion of the square shape.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As long as the outer face of the box is intact, the תפילין are כשר.

steps.title: Two torn walls is valid, three is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא sets a limit: two torn inner walls are allowed, but three make the תפילין פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: if two walls tore, the תפילין are valid. If three tore, they are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a different and more detailed rule. He counts how many inner walls have torn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא only looked at the outer surface. רב חסדא says the number of torn inner walls also matters. Up to two is fine, and three is too many.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
if two tore, they are valid;
phrases.notes: "Two" means two of the leather walls between the four compartments.

phrases.english: three, they are invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: נִפְסְקוּ שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion next to רב הונא's, based on how many walls tore.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two torn inner walls: כשר. Three torn inner walls: פסול.

steps.title: Two tears are valid only if they are not aligned
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits רב חסדא's rule: two tears are fine only when they are not aligned with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: when you said two torn walls are valid, that is only when they are not aligned with each other. If they are aligned with each other, the תפילין are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a condition to רב חסדא's rule about two torn walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two tears are not always allowed. If the two torn walls are not aligned with each other, the תפילין stay כשר. If they are aligned with each other, even two tears make them פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when, a formula that limits an earlier rule

phrases.english: Rava said:
That which you said, that two are valid,
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to רב חסדא's rule from the step before.

phrases.english: we said this only
when one is not aligned with the other;
but if one is aligned with the other, they are invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ שְׁתַּיִם כְּשֵׁירוֹת, לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב חסדא's rule that two torn walls are valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two torn walls are כשר only if they are not aligned with each other. If they are aligned, the תפילין are פסול.

steps.title: Aligned tears invalidate only new תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבא narrows the rule again: aligned tears make only new תפילין פסול, not old ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even the rule about aligned tears applies only to new תפילין. With old תפילין, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second limit, this time to the rule he just gave. Aligned tears are a problem only in new תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In new תפילין, aligned tears show that the leather itself is bad, so they are פסול. In old תפילין, the tears come from age and use, so they stay כשר. This sets up the next question: how do we know which תפילין count as new?

keyTerms.meaning: We have no problem with it

phrases.english: And even one aligned with the other
we said this only about new ones;
but with old ones, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזֶה כְּנֶגֶד זֶה נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּחַדְתָּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבא's own rule about aligned tears even further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Aligned tears make new תפילין פסול, but old תפילין stay כשר.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate limits here. First, two tears are a problem only if they are aligned. Second, even aligned tears are a problem only in new תפילין.

steps.title: How do we tell new תפילין from old?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף what counts as new and what counts as old.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: What counts as new תפילין, and what counts as old?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a practical question to define the terms רבא just used. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule depends on whether the תפילין are new or old. Age alone is not a clear measure. אביי wants a test that can actually be used.

keyTerms.meaning: What are they like? (How do we define them?)

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What are new ones like,
and what are old ones like?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמְיָין חַדְתָּתָא, וְהֵיכִי דָּמְיָין עַתִּיקָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the terms רבא used in the step before.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A test for telling new תפילין from old ones.

steps.title: The pull test for old and new
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers: if the leather springs back after being pulled, the תפילין are old. If it does not, they are new.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Whenever you hold the leather and pull it and it goes back into place, they are old. Otherwise, they are new.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a hands-on test. Pull the leather and see whether it goes back into place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is about how the leather behaves, not about how many years it has been in use. If the leather goes back into place, the תפילין count as old, so aligned tears are fine. If not, they count as new, and aligned tears make them פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes back into place, closes up again

steps.whatToRemember: Head-תפילין with torn inner walls: רב הונא says they are כשר while the outer face is whole. רב חסדא allows two tears but not three. רבא says two aligned tears are פסול, but only in new תפילין. Leather that goes back into place after a pull counts as old.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל הֵיכָא כִּי מִיתְּלֵי בֵּיהּ בְּשִׁלְחָא
phrases.english: Wherever, when one holds it by the leather and pulls,
and it goes back into place, they are old;
and the other, they are new.
phrases.notes: "The other" means the leather does not go back into place after the pull.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל הֵיכָא כִּי מִיתְּלֵי בֵּיהּ בְּשִׁלְחָא וַהֲדַר חָלֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leather that goes back into place after a pull counts as old. Leather that does not counts as new.
